title.value: Reinforcement Learning with Competitive Ensembles of Information-Constrained Primitives
title.justification: The title is directly stated in the first page of the paper.
title.quote: Reinforcement Learning with Competitive Ensembles of Information-Constrained Primitives

analysis.description: The paper proposes a method for reinforcement learning that structures policy into primitives without using a high-level meta-policy. Instead, each primitive decides based on the information it needs from the state, and a competition mechanism selects the most information-requesting primitive to act. This decentralized decision-making is shown to enhance generalization compared to both flat and hierarchical policies.

type.justification: The paper includes experimental demonstrations and comparisons with other methods, suggesting it is based on empirical studies.
type.quote: We experiment with both fixed and variable sets of primitives and show that our method allows for primitives to be added or removed during training, or recombined in new ways. Each primitive is represented by a differentiable, parameterized function approximator, such as a neural network.

name.justification: The paper focuses on teaching agents through reinforcement learning frameworks and experiments.
name.quote: Our goal is to learn a policy, composed of multiple primitive sub-policies, to maximize average returns over T-step interactions for a distribution of tasks.

name.justification: The paper presents an alternative to hierarchical reinforcement learning approaches by proposing decentralized decision-making primitives.
name.quote: However, hierarchical approaches rely on some form of learned high-level controller, which decides when to activate different components in the hierarchy.
